instructions: Filled in from manifest.template.json for the invoice-reconciliation exercise. See README.md in this folder for the full explanation of each entry.

development_tools_and_models.notes: Development tool: Claude Code (CLI), model Claude Opus 5, used throughout the build for all coding, planning, and testing work. No IDE plugin or extension was used alongside it.

plugins_and_extensions.notes: No editor plugin or browser extension was used. All work went through the Claude Code CLI directly.

application_models_and_parameters.notes: This is the in-application model call, separate from the development tool above. Model: us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0, called through classic AWS Bedrock (boto3 bedrock-runtime, invoke_model), region us-east-1. temperature = 0.0, for repeatable extraction on the same invoice image. max_tokens = 1024. Both model_id and region read from the BEDROCK_MODEL_ID and AWS_REGION environment variables first, falling back to these same values as defaults if the variables are unset. See configuration_records for the corrected client-class history (AnthropicBedrockMantle was tried first and found unusable on this account).

skills.notes: No skill was written for this exercise. The repository has three general-purpose skills under .claude/skills/ (fastapi-best-practices, modern-python-development, pytest-best-practices). These are reusable conventions, not exercise-specific work, and existed as organization-level patterns rather than being authored for this task. They are listed under agent_instructions_and_subagents because each subagent's frontmatter declares which of them it applies.

agent_instructions_and_subagents.notes: Four custom subagents, each scoped to one layer of the build. python-backend: FastAPI routes, Jinja2 templates, the headless batch command, the reconciliation rules engine, and the money-conversion module (skills: fastapi-best-practices, modern-python-development). sqlite-database: schema and data-access layer, integer-cents money columns, the correction audit trail (skills: modern-python-development). bedrock-extraction: the AWS Bedrock extraction call, the vision prompt, field parsing, and the credential-free response cache (skills: modern-python-development). testing-expert: feature-level acceptance tests mapped to functional-spec.md criteria, run once per feature rather than per slice (skills: pytest-best-practices). All four were genuinely invoked during the build, not drafted and left unused.

hooks_and_scripts.notes: No hook was configured for this exercise. .claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json contain no hooks key.

prompts_and_rules.notes: Project-level markdown files that directed the build: the domain rules for reconciliation and duplicate detection, the architecture decisions (stack, persistence, model choice), and the functional/technical spec and task breakdown for the reviewer-UI feature. These are ordinary repository files, not a separate prompt-injection mechanism, and are already committed at their normal paths.

tool_and_mcp_settings.notes: Two MCP servers are configured: awos-recruitment (a capability-discovery lookup used during agent setup, not during the invoice-reconciliation build itself) and aws-knowledge-mcp-server (AWS documentation lookup). Neither carries exercise-specific configuration beyond its connection URL, and both are visible in the committed .mcp.json at the repository root. No MCP server was written for this exercise.

permissions_and_environment_names.notes: Root .env.example lists the two environment variable names the application reads: AWS_REGION and BEDROCK_MODEL_ID, both optional overrides with in-code defaults (see application_models_and_parameters). No API key variable exists in this project: AWS credentials resolve through the standard AWS credential chain (SigV4), not an application-level secret. .claude/settings.local.json exists and holds a Bash command permission allowlist and an enabled-MCP-servers list; it is not exported here because its allowlist entries embed machine-specific absolute paths (this machine's home-directory name and a per-session scratchpad UUID), which are personal-machine detail rather than exercise configuration. .claude/settings.json (the shared, committed file) contains only the awos-marketplace registry source and is reproduced in full in README.md since it holds nothing sensitive.
